node.title: DLI cyclic conjugate-band primitive no-go
node.statement: Let n=8r and zeta have exact order n in characteristic greater than eight. The disjoint cyclic frequency bands F_2={2+8l} and F_6={6+8l} define identical binary null events, each of probability (36/256)^r. After antipodal first-owner deletion their primitive joint probability is (36^r-4^r)/256^r, so the joint-to-product ratio is (64/9)^r(1-9^-r), already 512/81>sqrt(16) at r=1 and exponential in r. This does not touch the official one-sided prefix, which contains no conjugate pair f,-f.
node.attack_surface: Check Fourier localization, equality of the order-eight conjugate equations, characteristic scope, 36 and 4 local counts, primitive subtraction, ratio normalization, and absence of conjugate pairs from the official prefix.
node.falsifier: A local binary word separating the two conjugate events, a mismatch in the 36/4 counts, or failure of the r=1 primitive ratio to exceed sqrt(16).
node.notes: This proves that primitivity plus arbitrary disjoint cyclic bands is still too weak. The surviving target-specific hypothesis is one-sided low-prefix geometry, together with nesting and ownership.
